title: When did OpenClaw come out, and who owns Clawdbot now?
h1: when did openclaw come out, and did openai buy it?
description: The project began as Clawd in November 2025. See when it became OpenClaw, what its creator announced about OpenAI and who looks after it today.
answer: **the openclaw name came out on 29 january 2026. the project began as clawd in november 2025.** moltbot was the name in between.[^2] on 14 february 2026, creator peter steinberger announced he was joining openai.[^3] openai didn't buy the project. the independent openclaw foundation launched on 8 july 2026.[^1]

review.by: lead agent: independent reviewer pass against seo/facts (4 reviewers), every finding applied, automated gate

og_line: the names changed. follow the dates.

sections.h: the names belong to one history
sections.md:
**clawd, moltbot and openclaw belong to the same project's story.** clawd began in november 2025. after anthropic's legal team requested a rename, moltbot followed. openclaw arrived on 29 january 2026.[^2] clawdbot also appears in a repository docker advisory.[^6]

match a tutorial's date, release and install instructions to the current docs before copying its commands.

**keep the rename, job move and foundation apart.** they answer different questions.

- **november 2025:** clawd begins. moltbot follows the rename request; the history gives no exact date.[^2]
- **29 january 2026:** the project announces the openclaw name.[^2]
- **14 february 2026:** peter steinberger announces his move to openai. he says openclaw will enter a foundation and stay independent.[^3]
- **8 july 2026:** the foundation launches as a us 501(c)(3) with full-time staff. it says openai committed to keeping the project open and independent.[^1]

sections.h: the creator joined openai; the project got a foundation
sections.md:
**february explains the new job; july explains who looks after openclaw.** the creator's post sets out his plans. the foundation announcement describes an independent organisation, rather than an acquisition or an openai product.[^1][^3]

the connection is real: the creator joined openai, and the foundation describes openai's commitment. ownership, support and safety guarantees don't follow from that connection.

**install the project as it exists today.** as of 12 november 2026, openclaw describes an open-source assistant for your computer or server, reached through chat apps. its repository uses mit.[^4][^5]

look at the current setup and upkeep before installing. the [alternatives guide](/alternatives/openclaw) compares the work involved. the [safety guide](/guides/is-openclaw-safe) separates published advisories, malicious skills and later security work.

sections.h: follow the headline back to its announcement
sections.md:
**the original announcement tells you what actually changed.** a creator's post explains their plans. a foundation post describes the organisation. the repository shows the license and code history.

for an acquisition claim, ask for an acquisition announcement. another retelling of the creator joining openai won't do.

for a clawd or moltbot setup guide, match its release to the current project site. old downloads, hosts and lookalike names still need that scrutiny.

faq.q: what is the difference between clawdbot and moltbot?
faq.a: **both names appear in openclaw's history.** the naming account goes from clawd to moltbot to openclaw. an older repository advisory also uses clawdbot.[^2][^6]
**peter steinberger is its creator.** he announced his move to openai on 14 february 2026.[^3]
**the foundation says yes.** its announcement calls the project open and independent and describes openai's commitment to that. this remained its position on 12 november 2026.[^1]

**the project's history gives november 2025 for clawd, without an exact release day for clawdbot.** the repository dates to 24 november 2025. that dates the repository, not a public release. the 29 january announcement introduced the openclaw name.[^5][^2]

steps: find the date on the guide or headline
read whether it says rename, job move or acquisition

mistakes.mistake: reading 'creator joins openai' as 'openai buys app'
mistakes.fix: look for an acquisition announcement. the cited posts describe different events.

mistakes.mistake: installing from a familiar old name
mistakes.fix: use the current project site and match the release the guide covers.

tip.text: a founder's next employer doesn't tell you who owns their earlier project.
